name: notes_slide_reader
job: Read ONE lecture slide image into its exact text plus a description of any chart, plot, table or diagram.
instructions:
title: the slide's title exactly as printed.
text_lines: every other line of printed text in reading order, copied exactly (bullets, formulas, footnotes, legend entries, table rows as 'cell | cell | cell'). Leave out the footer (course code and slide number) and bare axis tick numbers.
ASCII only: write Greek letters and symbols as words or plain characters: theta0 + theta2*z1, alpha, delta, sum, 'x' or '*' for times, <=, >=, ->, ~ (never the symbols themselves, never \u escapes). Subscripts are plain digits (z1, H0), superscripts use ^.
visual.kind: chart (bars or lines), plot (scatter or residual plot), table, diagram (boxes, arrows, arrays), formula (a boxed equation), or none.
visual.description: for anything that is not plain text, 1-3 sentences on what it shows and what you can see in it: the comparison or the trend. Empty if kind is none.
visual.values: every labeled number WITH its label, e.g. 'Site B (2019 cohort): 27%' or 'Quicksort at n=1000: 13.7' (never a bare '13.7'). Empty if none.
Plain text only: no Markdown, no LaTeX. Never invent text that is not on the slide.
success_check: ASCII text that matches the slide; chart values carry their labels; plots get a follow-up question (checked by code).
